problems.question: Calculate $\frac{3}{5} + \frac{1}{4}$. Express your answer in its simplest form.
Find the fraction $\frac{a}{b}$ (in simplest form) such that $\frac{1}{2} < \frac{a}{b} < \frac{2}{3}$ and $a + b = 20$.
problems.answer: We need $\frac{a}{b}$ such that $\frac{1}{2} < \frac{a}{b} < \frac{2}{3}$ and $a + b = 20$. So $a = 20 - b$. Inequalities: $\frac{1}{2} < \frac{20-b}{b} < \frac{2}{3}$. Left: $\frac{20-b}{b} > \frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow 2(20-b) > b \Rightarrow 40 - 2b > b \Rightarrow 40 > 3b \Rightarrow b < 13.33$ Right: $\frac{20-b}{b} < \frac{2}{3} \Rightarrow 3(20-b) < 2b \Rightarrow 60 - 3b < 2b \Rightarrow 60 < 5b \Rightarrow b > 12$ So $b = 13$, $a = 7$. Fraction: $\frac{7}{13}$. Check: $\frac{1}{2} = 0.5$, $\frac{7}{13} \approx 0.538$, $\frac{2}{3} \approx 0.667$. ✓

problems.question: Without using a calculator, find the value of $$\frac{1}{1 \times 2} + \frac{1}{2 \times 3} + \frac{1}{3 \times 4} + \dots + \frac{1}{99 \times 100}$$
problems.answer: Note that $\frac{1}{n(n+1)} = \frac{1}{n} - \frac{1}{n+1}$. So the sum telescopes: $$\left(\frac{1}{1} - \frac{1}{2}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{3}\right) + \dots + \left(\frac{1}{99} - \frac{1}{100}\right)$$ All intermediate terms cancel: $$= \frac{1}{1} - \frac{1}{100} = \frac{99}{100}$$
